findings.summary: The website exclusion counts every slash-bearing word as a path, so ordinary words, page URLs and the records-source fallback flip a website request into a fix
findings.evidence: `looks_like_path` accepts any word containing '/' that does not start with '/' (topics.rs:63-72); `request_text_touches` collects them over the whole text (title, body, acceptance), not only real paths. 'and/or', 'pass/fail' or 'https://.../page' are therefore 'paths' not in WEBSITE_PATHS, and the plan makes 'any other path' a fix. Website requests are the ones most likely to cite the published page URL (the audience rating's target is in the steward brief, audience.rs:125-127). When the model's words name no path, `StewardRequest::from_change` fills Files: from the change source, often a `records/` path (steward.rs:626-633), which also makes a website request a fix. The plan's criterion 3 fixtures use clean single-path texts, so the tests would pass while the owner's exclusion leaks in practice. Fix: Before checking WEBSITE_PATHS, drop touched words that contain '://' or do not exist at the base commit (entry_of already has `path_exists`; pass it into the classifier, or apply the website guard in drain.rs where the lookup lives). Add table cases to the `is_website_request`/`fix_requests_of` tests: a studies request whose body holds 'and/or', one that cites a page URL, and one whose only path is the `records/` source fallback; each must not be a fix.

findings.summary: The claim that gate-line classification 'matches the existing guaranteed-turn rule' is false
findings.evidence: `improvement_of` (hestia.rs:973-1007) collects steward-channel requests, repeated-cause requests, throughput design requests and spec requests; it never looks at `Gate under review:` lines. Gate-review requests get no guaranteed turn today, so the fix set and the improvement set will disagree. Fix: Correct the risk text and D181: gate-review requests are ranked as fixes but have no guaranteed turn. Or add them to `improvement_of` and say so, with a test.

findings.summary: Two definitions of the website's source paths can drift apart
findings.evidence: `OUTCOME_PATHS = ["studies/", "xtask/", ".github/workflows/pages.yml"]` already defines what the explainer page is built from; the new list is narrower and nothing ties the two together. Fix: Add a test (in athena-cli, which can see both) that every WEBSITE_PATHS entry starts with an OUTCOME_PATHS prefix, or name the deliberate difference in both doc comments and D181.

findings.summary: `fix_requests_of` runs on every `plan_entry` call, which the read and vet passes make once per item, not once per call
findings.evidence: `plan_entry` is called per job by the read pass (drain.rs:2282) and by vet (drain.rs:2078); each call would rebuild the whole fix set, including the introspection scan in `improvement_of`. The plan's cost argument covers `queue()` only. Likely small beside the records load each call already does (estimate, not measured). Fix: State the per-call cost in the risk, or compute the fix set once per pass and pass it in.

findings.summary: The text says 'four steward-channel requests' but lists three
findings.evidence: It lists studies, site.rs and shard.rs requests; the expected order `[shard_request, feature, studies_request, site_request]` has four entries counting the person request. Fix: Say three steward requests plus one person request.

summary: Read: plan.rs:740-792 (the sort at 783 sits after the best-tier and dependency filters), drain.rs entry_of/queue/plan_entry/improvement (4339-4572), hestia.rs improvement_of, is_waiting_request, GATE_LINE and open_gate_request, steward.rs improvement_requests, StewardRequest and RequestQueue::apply and decide, the steward's kind mapping (1045-1048), topics.rs looks_like_path, request_text_touches and plan_entry, reading.rs queue (channel cli), and the queue_steward_request call sites in tests/drain.rs. The core design is sound: one sort-key change inside the best effective tier, a classifier based on the steward channel and Hestia's record links, and well-reasoned removal of the approved-work-item route (approved items are always Proposals). The dependents list matches the readers I found, and every order sentence that would become false is updated. The one major problem is the website/study exclusion. It treats every slash-bearing word in the request text as a path and promotes any non-website 'path', so 'and/or', page URLs and the `records/` source fallback would rank website requests as fixes. The plan's clean fixtures would not catch this. Filtering to paths that exist at the base commit, and adding those cases to the tests, fixes it. Minor: gate-review requests are not part of the guaranteed turn, contrary to one risk statement; two website path lists can drift apart; the fix set is recomputed on every plan_entry call.
